1: Based on the k-NN results of the nearest neighboring value, the suggested customer would decline the loan option. The majority of loan options are declined, so this appears to be a very feasible outcome by random chance. 

2. K controls the bias:variance trade-off. Making a small K offers flexibility, low bias, and high variance, which leads to overfitting. Conversely, a large K will run higher bias and lower variance to push underfitting. When a dataset is imbalanced (480/5000), a large K will drown out the minority.

3. Show confusion matrix

4. Best K is still determined to be K=1 at 0.9635 and results do not change, still showing the loan option being declined.

5. The difference shown at K=1 is that accuracy devolves from Train to Validate to Test. Part of this is likely due to a reduced data set. The Train data exhibits no mismatches for prediction to result, but even though there are less total values in the Test set, it yields the highest mismatched predictions:results. Because the best bias is such a low value, the model is working with extreme low bias and class imbalance is still high.
```{r}
# Load packages
library(caret)
library(fastDummies)
library(class)

# Load dataset 
UniversalBank <- read.csv("UniversalBank.csv")

# Remove unused variables
UniversalBank <- UniversalBank[, !(names(UniversalBank) %in% c("ID", "ZIP.Code"))]

# Handle extra Education variables with dummies
UniversalBank <- dummy_cols(
  UniversalBank,
  select_columns = "Education",
  remove_first_dummy = FALSE,
  remove_selected_columns = TRUE
)

# Set reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Train the model for 60% / p = .6; y = target variable
train_index <- createDataPartition(
  UniversalBank$Personal.Loan,
  p = 0.60,
  list = FALSE
)

train_data <- UniversalBank[train_index, ]
valid_data <- UniversalBank[-train_index, ]

# Normalize / Scale
predictor_names <- setdiff(names(train_data), "Personal.Loan")

preproc <- preProcess(
  train_data[, predictor_names],
  method = c("center", "scale")
)

train_x <- predict(preproc, train_data[, predictor_names])
valid_x <- predict(preproc, valid_data[, predictor_names])

########## 1: Create Sample Record ##########
new_customer <- data.frame(
  Age = 40,
  Experience = 10,
  Income = 84,
  Family = 2,
  CCAvg = 2,
  Mortgage = 0,
  Securities.Account = 0,
  CD.Account = 0,
  Online = 1,
  CreditCard = 1,
  Education_1 = 0,
  Education_2 = 1,
  Education_3 = 0
)

new_customer <- predict(preproc, new_customer)

pred <- knn(
  train = train_x,
  test = new_customer,
  # Define Success factor of 0=declined and 1 = accepted
  cl = factor(train_data$Personal.Loan),
  # Determine nearest neighbor accepting or declining
  k = 1,
  prob = TRUE
)

# Convert results to table
result <- data.frame(
  Prediction = pred,
  Label = ifelse(pred == 1, "Accept", "Decline"),
  Confidence = round(attr(pred, "prob") * 100, 2)
)

print(result)

########## 3: Confusion matrix of K ##########
# Find the best K
k_values <- seq(1, 25, 2)
accuracy <- rep(0, length(k_values))

for (i in seq_along(k_values)) {
  pred <- knn(
    train = train_x,
    test = valid_x,
    cl = train_data$Personal.Loan,
    k = k_values[i]
  )
  
  accuracy[i] <- mean(pred == valid_data$Personal.Loan)
}

results <- data.frame(k = k_values, accuracy = accuracy)
results

best_k <- results$k[which.max(results$accuracy)]
best_k

# Predict again using the best K
best_pred <- knn(
  train = train_x,
  test = valid_x,
  cl = train_data$Personal.Loan,
  k = best_k
)

# Confusion Matrix
conf_matrix <- table(
  Predicted = best_pred,
  Actual = valid_data$Personal.Loan
)

# Confusion Matrix table visual

cm <- table(
  Predicted = best_pred,
  Actual = valid_data$Personal.Loan
)

cm_df <- as.data.frame(cm)

cm_df$Predicted <- ifelse(cm_df$Predicted == 1, "Accept", "Decline")
cm_df$Actual <- ifelse(cm_df$Actual == 1, "Accept", "Decline")

names(cm_df)[3] <- "Count"

cm_df

########## 4: Classify previous customer with best K ##########
new_customer_4 <- predict(preproc, new_customer)
pred_4 <- knn(
  train = train_x,
  test = new_customer_4,
  # Define Success factor of 0=declined and 1 = accepted
  cl = train_data$Personal.Loan,
  # Determine nearest neighbor accepting or declining
  k = best_k,
  prob = TRUE
)

# Convert results to table
result_4 <- data.frame(
  Prediction = pred_4,
  Label = ifelse(pred_4 == 1, "Accept", "Decline"),
  Confidence = round(attr(pred_4, "prob") * 100, 2)
)

print(result_4)

########## 5: Repartition with best K 50:30:20 ##########
n <- nrow(UniversalBank)
# Split into 50/50
train_index <- createDataPartition(UniversalBank$Personal.Loan, p = 0.50, list = FALSE)
train_data <- UniversalBank[train_index, ]

temp_data <- UniversalBank[-train_index, ]
# Split 50 into 60/40
valid_index <- createDataPartition(temp_data$Personal.Loan, p = 0.60, list = FALSE)
valid_data <- temp_data[valid_index, ]
test_data <- temp_data[-valid_index, ]

# Make predictions
predictor_names <- setdiff(names(train_data), "Personal.Loan")

train_x <- train_data[, predictor_names]
valid_x <- valid_data[, predictor_names]
test_x  <- test_data[, predictor_names]

# Scale for training only
preproc <- preProcess(train_x, method = c("center", "scale"))

train_x <- predict(preproc, train_x)
valid_x <- predict(preproc, valid_x)
test_x  <- predict(preproc, test_x)

# Fit best K
train_pred <- knn(train_x, train_x, train_data$Personal.Loan, k = best_k)
valid_pred <- knn(train_x, valid_x, train_data$Personal.Loan, k = best_k)
test_pred  <- knn(train_x, test_x,  train_data$Personal.Loan, k = best_k)

# New confusion matrix
# Train
cm_train <- table(Predicted = train_pred, Actual = train_data$Personal.Loan)

cm_train_df <- as.data.frame(cm_train)
names(cm_train_df)[3] <- "Count"

cm_train_df

# Validate
cm_train <- table(Predicted = valid_pred, Actual = valid_data$Personal.Loan)

cm_train_df <- as.data.frame(cm_train)
names(cm_train_df)[3] <- "Count"

cm_train_df

# Test
cm_train <- table(Predicted = test_pred, Actual = test_data$Personal.Loan)

cm_train_df <- as.data.frame(cm_train)
names(cm_train_df)[3] <- "Count"

cm_train_df

# Nice table
data.frame(
  Set = c("Train", "Validate", "Test"),
  Accuracy = c(
    mean(train_pred == train_data$Personal.Loan),
    mean(valid_pred == valid_data$Personal.Loan),
    mean(test_pred == test_data$Personal.Loan)
  )
)
```
